name.en: Official USD/EUR exchange rate (Italian lira before 1999)

unit.en: EUR per USD (lira converted to EUR)

note.vi: Nguon: World Bank, ty gia chinh thuc binh quan nam (PA.NUS.FCRF). Truoc 1999 la lia Y (ITL) tren USD, quy doi sang EUR theo ty gia khong the dao nguoc 1936,27 ITL = 1 EUR (co dinh tu 1/1/1999). Tu 1999 la ty gia EUR/USD thuc te, giong het chuoi cua Phap vi ca hai nuoc chung dong Euro.
note.en: Source: World Bank official exchange rate, period average (PA.NUS.FCRF). Pre-1999 figures are Italian lira (ITL) per USD, converted to EUR at the irrevocable rate of 1936.27 ITL = 1 EUR (fixed 1 Jan 1999). From 1999 onward this is the actual EUR/USD rate, identical to France's series since both share the euro.

name.vi: Luong trung binh hang nam (vi khong co luong toi thieu quoc gia)
name.en: Average annual wage (Italy has no statutory national minimum wage)

note.vi: QUAN TRONG: Y la mot trong 5 nuoc EU (cung Dan Mach, Ao, Phan Lan, Thuy Dien) khong co luong toi thieu theo luat dinh; muc san luong duoc thoa uoc lao dong tap the theo nganh (CCNL) quy dinh rieng cho tung nganh, khong co con so quoc gia duy nhat. Do do muc nay dung luong binh quan nam (gia hien hanh, toan bo lao dong lam cong) theo OECD thay the, nhu huong dan khi khong co luong toi thieu chinh thuc. Day la luong GOP (gross), khong phai luong rong.
note.en: IMPORTANT: Italy is one of 5 EU countries (with Denmark, Austria, Finland, Sweden) without a statutory minimum wage; wage floors are set sector-by-sector through collective bargaining agreements (CCNL), so there is no single national figure. This item therefore uses the OECD average annual wage (current prices, all employees) as the substitute, as instructed when no official minimum wage exists. This is gross (pre-tax) pay, not take-home pay.

name.vi: Gia vang (LBMA, cuoi nam) theo gram

note.vi: Gia vang giao ngay LBMA (London) cuoi nam. Day la gia toan cau quy sang EUR, giong het chuoi cua Phap va cac nuoc dong Euro khac vi vang duoc dinh gia theo USD/EUR toan cau, khong co gia rieng cho tung nuoc. Truoc 1999 quy doi tu gia lia (hoac mac/franc) sang EUR theo ty gia khong the dao nguoc; gia ban le tai Y co them thue/phi gia cong nen cao hon.
note.en: LBMA London spot gold price at year-end. This is a global price converted to EUR, identical to France's series and other euro-area countries since gold is priced in global USD/EUR, not country by country. Pre-1999 figures use the irrevocable conversion rate; actual Italian retail prices are higher due to dealer premiums and fabrication fees.

name.vi: Gia Big Mac (trung binh khu vuc dong Euro)

note.vi: The Economist chi cong bo mot muc gia Big Mac duy nhat cho ca khu vuc dong Euro (ma 'EUZ'), khong tach rieng cho Y; gia nay dai dien chung cho ca khu vuc, co the chenh lech vai % so voi gia nieu yet thuc te tai cac thanh pho Y. Moi diem lay tu lan khao sat dau nam.
note.en: The Economist only publishes a single Big Mac price for the whole euro area ('EUZ'), not broken out for Italy specifically; this price is a euro-area proxy and can differ by a few percent from actual menu prices in Italian cities. One point per year from the first survey wave of that year.

name.vi: Gia nha o trung binh toan quoc theo m2
name.en: Average national residential property price per sqm

note.vi: Du lieu Nomisma (qua CEIC) chi co tu 2008; khong tim duoc chuoi gia nha binh quan toan quoc dang tin cay cho 1986-2007 trong pham vi nghien cuu nay, nen bo trong doan nay thay vi uoc tinh. Day la gia binh quan toan quoc (ca can ho/nha), khong rieng thanh pho lon (gia tai Milano/Roma cao hon nhieu, vd Milano ~3.337 EUR/m2 nam 2022).
note.en: Nomisma data (via CEIC) only starts in 2008; no reliable national average housing price series for 1986-2007 was found within this research pass, so that span is left blank rather than estimated. This is the nationwide average (all dwelling types), not specific to major cities (Milan/Rome prices are much higher, e.g. Milan ~EUR 3,337/sqm in 2022).
